Messages.Body:
I threw this up on the VTES-L list already...but this is for those who aren't
on it. This is a 6CL deck. The original version had a Memories and a
Blood Doll instead of the two Barrens. Also the Laptop Computers were
a replacement for more Computer Hacking. The Sport Bikes replaced more
another Arson, PF, and 2 Dodges. I've toyed with variations using Ambush
or Delaying Tactics (or Surprise Influence).

Using pre-7/7 rules, I've had no problem sweeping small tables with this
deck since I'm able to concentrate my Memories better and I've had no
problem burning vampires with PF. I'm going to try it out on a JOL game
since that will be the most adverse conditions for the deck.

I'm interested to see how the rest of the text of PF works out. If I hit a
vampire down to zero and use PF, they're going to go to torpor as soon
as they have to hunt. With enough weenies at my disposal (or Nephandus)
burning vampires in torpor should be pretty much risk-free.

The deck construction uses the same formula that I use for all my decks:
12 vampire crypt, 90 card library containing 20 master cards.

Noal

Whoo, now that's a lot of Hunting Grounds. These are probably all good

Love that cycling. Some Effective Managements (or Info Highway) might go
well in this deck too.

I don't know if I'd really use the Knights or the Slashers here (or
especially the Loyal Street Gang). Allies that cost pool but have neither
a built in Rush nor a built in bleed strike me as a little sketchy compared
to vampires of the same cost. Arms Dealers are good, but clearly you
should have a Talbot's Chainsaw in here for them to fetch when Ambrosius
comes up. ;-)

The rest are all pretty good I think. I quite like the Renegade Garou
and Muddled Vampire Hunter in this kind of deck as well. (I was waiting
to comment on this deck until today because I was going to try out my
own take on an ally-abuse deck last night... which I did but unfortunately
I never got off the ground so my playtesting hasn't been very helpful yet.)
My version has more Giovanni though, so as to use (in theory) Compel
the Spirit to retrieve my expensive allies after they get killed.

: #Retainers

: Charnas the Imp
: Ghoul Escort
: Jackie Therman
: (2) J.S. Simmons, Esq.
: Tasha Morgan
: (2) Mr. Winthrop

I like all of these, although I'm not sure how useful Jackie Therman is
when you're not playing any ranged strikes. (Unless you're playing that
allies can recruit retainers? It had never even occurred to me that they
might be able to until the recent discussion here.)

: #Actions

: (6) Computer Hacking
: (3) Arson

I already mentioned Compel the Spirit; I would also recommend some Clan
Impersonations here - that way you don't have to rely solely on getting
out the right vampires to be able to recruit and play hunting grounds.

: #Combat

: (6) Dodge
: (6) Fake Out
: (6) Pulled Fangs

Always good choices, especially with the abusive old Pulled Fangs. ;-)

: #Equipment

: (5) Laptop Computer
: (4) Sport Bike

Also good. Again, I think you're required by law in 39 states to use a
Talbot's Chainsaw if you have Ambrosius. And if you do go for the Garou
angle, you must also add an RPG Launcher and a Hawg.

Josh

Messages.Body:
In article <7059l2$7kr$1...@nnrp1.dejanews.com>, Dhar...@yahoo.com wrote:

>> Whoo, now that's a lot of Hunting Grounds. These are probably all good
>> though; the HG/Blood Doll madness could work out well.
>
>Yep. Allies are expensive...gotta pay for them.

You will get back the pool, trust me.
Dan Hollis <Daniel....@Dartmouth.EDU> has a great HG/Blood Doll pool
gain machine going on in JOL 67. It was essentially a weenie vote deck with
pool gain, but boy is it hard to bleed that guy. He gets back more pool
than I can take out of him each turn, and I have two Pulsed minions! I must
say though that he does use a lot more Blood Dolls than you do, but 6 would
still be pretty effective.

Just remember though, if you want to go with pool gain and allies, try and
get some Autarkis Persecutions to pass. It does count all those lovely
allies you got under your control. It would be hard to pass though,
especially as your predator wouldn't like to see you get back some 20 or 40
pool a turn. If you do put in APs, you'll need some Bewitching Orations,
and Bribes might not be such a bad idea, after all, everyone will be
getting some pool anyway.

Maybe a few Anarch Revolts could fit into the deck too. Whether or not you
put in the votes, you have the Blood Dolls to survive when the Anarchs come
back your way.

>> My version has more Giovanni though, so as to use (in theory) Compel
>> the Spirit to retrieve my expensive allies after they get killed.
>
>*nods* Not a bad idea. I'm just not sure if I could fit them in.

Well, in that case you just make your first deck, and once your playgroup
has learned what it can do, go with the suggestions and things that didn't
go in the first deck. Keep them guessing and wondering, that's the main
trick. Same old strategy, but whole new fearsome look.

>> when you're not playing any ranged strikes. (Unless you're playing that

If you want to give your vamps some maneuvers, give them Deer Rifles. It
might only stings, but it still stings. And it's hard to destroy with a
ranged strike.

>> I already mentioned Compel the Spirit; I would also recommend some Clan
>> Impersonations here - that way you don't have to rely solely on getting
>> out the right vampires to be able to recruit and play hunting grounds.
>
>*nods* Not a bad idea...but there's little room for them. Some of the fun
>is that the deck is entirely unpredictable. Not a tournament winning deck,
>but one that's fun to play among friends.

Definitively in deck #2 then. With those Giovanni turned whatever you need.

>> : (6) Pulled Fangs
>>
>> Always good choices, especially with the abusive old Pulled Fangs. ;-)
>
>Esp. with Memories out....

Yep yep yep. I always liked that card, just didn't find the deck to play
it. Your only real worry would be Corruption and other steal ally/retainer
cards. Unfortunately, the clans making best use of these have obfuscate.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <7087rh$gmd$1...@nnrp1.dejanews.com>, Dhar...@yahoo.com writes

>Keep in mind that this is an Allies deck.

I think the point being made here isn't that you could make a much, much
better allies deck, but that, in general, allies decks don't do so well
and that you would be more competitive with a weenie deck.

Of course, if you're not going for competitive that doesn't matter but,
in general, a 2 or 3 capacity vampire is going to help you a lot more
than a 2 or 3 pool ally (who you've already had to pay for a vampire for
to get out in any case).

Problems with allies:

1) They (generally) only use Disciplineless cards which are normally
poor and very simple

2) They cannot heal life (generally)

3) When they lose life, they are burned - a vampire needs other actions
to be taken, or a much more difficult set of conditions to be reached
(Decap/Amaranth with Blood Hunt vote problems/Gangrel
Conspiracy/Diablerie and to hell with it).

On the plus side, you can get cool special abilities and a lot better
hand damage. Renegade Garou rocks, in my opinion, especially with a
source of aggravated damage. Hit a vampire with two blood on them once
with his 2 damage, then once with his two damage and a Wooden Stake and
they're burned (2 damage to 0 blood, 3rd normal damage wounds him and so
4th point of damage - aggro - requires him to burn a blood to prevent
destruction since he is already wounded). Lovely against weenies and
cool anyway.

However, since you *are* playing an ally deck, these are secondary
points. The major problems with this deck, as I see them, are the pool
cost and the spread of clans.

For any given ally, you have to get out a vampire and then the ally -
effectively doubling their cost if you concentrate on allies. However,
this would not be a problem so much if you were, say, playing a Brujah
ally deck. Get out Lupo and run with her only. The problem with this
deck is it has too many clans. You can't really afford Clan
Impersonation with these vamps - it would slow things down unbearably.
However, you need it because of the spread of the clans - 6 in total.

My advice would be:

1) Add some more pool gain if you can - Blood Dolls don't cost a Master
Phase Action once you've played them, so toy with that.

2) Slim down the clans. This might allow you to toy with the master
slots freed up by losing the Hunting Grounds for 1 although you may like
to double up on the other ones.

3) In the process of slimming down, try and focus a little more on one
area. By doing bleed, combat and intercept, the deck becomes a bit
"mushy". Jack of all trades, master of none and all that jazz. Maybe
throw out the Brujah allies and build up on the good bleeders, or go the
other way round. How you choose here is up to you.

1x KRCG News Radio (light intercept is often handy)
1x Morgue Hunting Ground (pool/blood gain)
1x Powerbase Chicago (pool gain)
3x Memories of Mortality (didn't think this was crucial enough to play lots..)

minions:

2x Clan Impersonation (sounded better than it worked)
3x Whispers from the Dead (card recycling - Carlotta's probably enough)
8x Compel the Spirit (hard to get the right balance)
3x Grave Robbing (good in theory though often blocked)

Spectral Divination (probably not worth the 1 blood)
5x Cloak the Gathering (try to get the recruit/compels through)
2x Conditioning (a little extra bleed power)

5x Deflection (bounce can be handy; didn't see much heavy bleed though)
4x Wake with Evening's Freshness (to go with the Deflections)

7x Fake Out (allies need maneuvers)
3x Dodge (for allies and vamps)
3x Dead End Alley (presses for the Garou mostly)
6x Spiritual Intervention (combat defense for the Giovanni)

3x IR Goggles (more manuevers - possibly excessive)
Hawg (the Garou thing)
RPG Launcher (Garou again)
Talbot's Chainsaw (requisite Ambrosius combo; hasn't come up yet)

2x Guiseppe Gravedigger (not good enough)
5x Renegade Garou (too many, probably)
Gypsies (not bad but not amazing)
Leonardo Mortician (not great but not expensive either)
Scapelli Mechanic (hard to say, haven't actually played him)
3x Muddled Vampire Hunter (good when he shows up)
Ambrosius Ferryman (also hasn't shown up)
Order of Hermes Cabal (and neither have they)

---

changes made since then:

removed: Vast Wealth, 2 Sudden Reversal, 1 Dead End Alley, 2 Clan
Impersonation, 3 Whispers from the Dead, 1 Compel the Spirit, 1 Spectral
Divination, 1 IR Goggles, 1 Hawg, 1 RPG Launcher, 1 Guiseppe Gravedigger,
1 Powerbase Chicago, 1 Renegade Garou.

added: 2 Blood Doll (5), 1 Obfuscate (3), 1 Grave Robbing (4), 4 Cloak the
Gathering (9), 2 Dodge (5), 3 Trap (3), 1 Ivory Bow (1), 1 Possession (1),
1 Zoo Hunting Ground (1), 1 Asylum Hunting Ground (1).

---

My experience was that stacking up stuff onto the allies took way too much
time. My Garou needed to be killing stuff *now*, not going out and
buying himself a Hawg and an RPG launcher so he can kick more ass later.
For the same reason, Clan Impersonations are too slow (and not very
reliable). The added Cloaks are partly paranoia from having two Compels
blocked in a row (by an Assamite no less). 5 Garou looks like just
being too much - I kept discarding Garous. So I added a little pool
gain (like the multiple Hunting Ground idea), reduced the equipment, and
hopefully it'll play a little better now.

(So far, in four games, I think I've gotten one or two VPs total. It's
just not been working out very well. In most cases, I just wound up
slain before I could get my allies on the road. I'm not sure what
exactly to do about that. Maybe some Effective Managements would help
in terms of being more able to get the right clans up quickly enough,
but I'm not sure what I would cut for them.)

Josh

Yeah, and now that I'm his predator, he doesn't have the good grace to be
scared of my "Evil Petting Zoo" Tremere tha/cel/ani (<--ani!!!) rush deck.
Admittedly, this game is the testing ground from which it will be tuned, but
I think it's pretty nasty...and I'll post it in the future, sometime...

In all seriousness, replying to the crypt selection, I admit that I have seen
Michael Beer's proficiency in deck building online here, and have recieved a
bunch of good advice from him (lots about Assamites, I believe...), but I
have to agree with Noal that the larger vampires are valid selections. I've
seen this deck prey, and it was hostile-voted down on the...4th or 5th turn,
I think, by a grand or grand-grand prey ( where was Sorrow relative to you
Noal?) before he could get any farther. With using the whaddyacallem's for
the 2 blood to a younger uncontrolled vampire (especially with the Marijava
Ghouls), he doesn't really have to worry about pool much, and it's nice to
have a couple of older vampires...oh, and I think that adding in Auspex would
dilute the deck too much...I don't agree with Michael that he should have a
little for emergencies. All the deck needs is the presence...admittedly,
it's single-minded, but it's quite scary. The vampires are small enough in
general to not have to worry about losing them, and you can just bleed and
bleed and bleed. And the vote defense is handy. As I understand it, JOL is
typically a high-vote environment, but I have only seen a couple of votes
that couldn't have gone either way with a Dread Gaze thrown in. As I've
seen, most vote decks either rely on titled vampires *or* lots of Bewitching
Oration, etc. and not both. (Note: I said *rely* on, not use...most decks
seem to try to use both...)...and most of those votes came later in the game,
after voting dominance had been clearly established...Like Sorrow with his 80
million votes...

Oh yeah, Go Fun Decks!!! Once I've got the Smudge gets 7 Hand Damage deck
right, I'll post it again...I know at least a couple people were
interested...and if anyone wants to send me (or trade) extra Gangrel Revels
and Art of Pain (and Raptors), I'm looking for them, and I should just start
another post, but I'm too lazy...I'm still looking for @ 6 cards from
Sabbat...Hidden Pathways, Mind Rape, Succubus, Twisting the Knife, Gang
Territory, and Gangrel Conspiracy...got all sets (few V:TES) to trade, and
70+ Sabbat rares...

Xian
